captures.what_is_new: Commission press release IP/26/2407: the Commission presented its proposal for a Digital Fairness Act (a major update of EU consumer protection rules for online shopping), with a revision of the Consumer Protection Cooperation Regulation (direct powers to investigate and fine in large cross-border cases) and a simplification directive amending the Consumer Rights Directive. Key novelties it lists: a ban on manipulative 'dark patterns' (e.g. fake 'almost sold out' claims); clear pricing for purchases in virtual in-app currencies and dynamic pricing for cultural and sports events; limits on addictive design, gambling-like features for minors, personalised ads and prices; easier cancellation; a right to communicate with a human in customer service; and 'clear rights when using an AI agent to buy products on their behalf'. The Commission says businesses expect to save EU consumers up to EUR 13.7 billion a year. Next steps: the proposals will be discussed by the European Parliament and the Council. The Q&A (QANDA/26/2408) explains dark patterns and enforcement; it does not mention AI agents.
